bugs.criterion: Images, favicon and mobile performance foundations are present
bugs.description: Horizontal overflow on /about at 390px mobile viewport: document.documentElement.scrollWidth=429 > clientWidth=390. Root cause isolated via page.evaluate bounding-rect scan: an ARTICLE panel ('rounded-[2rem] border ... bg-[#eef2ff] p-7 sm:p-10', the 'The Person You Brief' / compliance content card) renders with right edge at x=429, overflowing the 390px viewport by ~39px, dragging the whole document width with it. A decorative absolute-positioned circle (right-[-7rem] size-80) also extends past the viewport but is intentionally off-canvas decoration, not the scroll-width driver - the ARTICLE panel is the actual cause.
bugs.evidence: run_browser_script(navigation-responsive-links): expect(hasOverflow=true).toBe(false) failed twice in a row (not flaky) on page.goto('/about') at 390x844. Cross-check: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:3000/about -> 200 (backend/page serving is healthy, confirming this is a frontend CSS layout bug, not a data/backend fault). Direct page.evaluate offender scan confirms the overflowing element and its bounding rect (left=22.6, right=429.4) against viewport width 390.

action_items.description: Constrain the /about content-card ARTICLE panels (compliance/work-brief sections, classes including 'rounded-[2rem] border ... p-7 sm:p-10') to the viewport width on small screens (e.g. add max-w-full/overflow-hidden or reduce horizontal padding at the sm breakpoint) so /about has no horizontal scroll at 390px, matching the criterion already satisfied by other pages (home, mobile-accessible-responsive check).
